requirements.evidence: Contract mostly present: enums (app/Enums/TicketChannel.php:5-10, TicketStatus.php:5-9), InactiveQueueException extends RuntimeException, IssueTicket rejects negative priority (IssueTicket.php:20-22), locks and re-reads the queue (IssueTicket.php:25-29), write-once saving hook (Ticket.php:31-44), call() with LogicException/AuthorizationException (Ticket.php:72-89), migrations with cascades, unique (queue_id, code) and the recommended index (tickets migration:24-25). Gaps: the retry loop (IssueTicket.php:34-53) runs inside the same DB::transaction, so on PostgreSQL a 23505 aborts the transaction and every retry fails; nextCode (Ticket.php:57-70) takes the last valid code still present, so deleting the latest ticket (A003) reuses its number; the factory assigns codes in afterMaking (TicketFactory.php:34-40), so `->count(2)->forQueue($q)->create()` makes both A001 before saving and violates the unique index; docs/business-rules.md is not updated even though the task asks for it.

conventions.evidence: Domain write is an Action (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php) and models set $fillable via #[Fillable] (Queue.php:11, Ticket.php:14). But no test at all is shipped, against 'No production code without a test'; authorization in Ticket::call is an ad hoc membership check (`$user->membershipFor(...)`, Ticket.php:78-82) rather than a policy/gate; docs/business-rules.md is not touched and docs/database-schema.md only changes its intro sentence (database-schema.md:3), so the queues/tickets tables are not documented.

security.evidence: Calling is restricted to entity members (Ticket.php:78-82), and the ticket stays unchanged on rejection because the check runs before any assignment. Fillable lists are explicit. Minor: Ticket fillable includes status/called_by_user_id (Ticket.php:14), which future HTTP code could mass-assign, and authorization is not centralised in a policy. No HTTP surface in this change.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no files under tests/; none of the code-sequence edge cases, inactive-queue rejection, write-once, single-call or authorization paths are tested.

simplicity.evidence: Code is mostly direct and small. nextCode loads and regex-scans every code in the queue on each issuance (Ticket.php:59-63) instead of reading only what it needs; the retry loop adds machinery that cannot work inside a single transaction (IssueTicket.php:30-53).

readability.evidence: Core classes are clear and well named. However the diff adds four junk files with corrupted names containing newlines and `content">` (change.diff:96, 128, 161) whose contents don't even match their names (a TicketChannel-named file contains InactiveQueueException). Inconsistent `\LogicException` inline FQCN vs imported exceptions (Ticket.php:40, 74).

scope.evidence: Besides the requested files, the change commits four stray artifact files under app/Enums and app/Exceptions with garbage paths (change.diff:96-177), apparently left over from broken tool calls. Everything else serves the task.

issues.explanation: No Pest/PHPUnit tests are shipped for any of the new behaviour, which the project's TDD convention requires and which leaves code sequencing, write-once, single-call and authorization untested.
Four junk files with newline-laden names and mismatched contents are committed; they're tool-call artifacts that must be removed.

The unique-collision retry runs inside the same transaction, so on PostgreSQL the first unique violation aborts the transaction and the retries cannot succeed. Under MySQL repeatable read, nextCode would also re-read the same snapshot, so the retry doesn't really work.
The task explicitly requires updating both docs. business-rules.md is untouched and database-schema.md only changes its intro line, without describing the queues/tickets tables.
The next code comes from the last valid code still in the table, so deleting the most recent ticket (e.g. A003) makes its number reused, contrary to 'deleting a ticket does not reuse its number'.
Codes are allocated in afterMaking, before any instance is saved, so creating several tickets in one factory call (count(2)->forQueue($q)->create()) gives all of them A001 and hits the unique index.
Authorization for calling a ticket is an inline membership check in the model instead of going through a policy/gate as the conventions require.
nextCode plucks every code in the queue on each issuance, which grows linearly with queue history.
LogicException is referenced inline as \LogicException while other exceptions are imported, which is inconsistent.

review.summary: The change adds queues/tickets migrations, models, enums, factories, the IssueTicket action, the write-once hook and Ticket::call, covering most of the contract. However it ships no tests at all, commits four corrupted stray files, leaves business-rules.md not updated, and has correctness gaps in the collision retry, code reuse after deleting the last ticket and multi-create factory codes, so it needs substantial rework before approval.
